chapter: Biddle, Durham and early road shows
title: Playing in a medicine show band
summary: A four-piece band played fast marches while a doctor sold a dollar-a-bottle tonic, staying three to four weeks in each town.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: So, that's how I got with the medicine show.
Oh, when you left the Hippodrome you went with a medicine show.
I went with the medicine show and I played with the medicine show.
What did you do in the medicine -- what kind of music did you play in a medicine show? Was that like a carnival?

No. This was just a -- this man -- he would sell medicine and he'd have -- to my idea, I think he would have a lot of chicken entrails in a bottle, in alcohol or something like that, and he would tell them that

these are parasites that he got -- you take this medicine and we would get it out and one of those things and he was selling the medicine for a dollar a bottle. And then he would talk and talk and talk. His name was Dr. -- I've forgotten his name -- Dr. somebody. But, anyway, strike up the band. And we'd strike up the band and then he started to selling this medicine. Only going for a dollar a bottle. I don't think I have but a few left. And the people was crowded around this thing. And, you know, we would start to playing. We play real fast music -- ra-ta-ra-ta -- one of those things. And while we're playing, he's selling medicine. He -- his helper was opening those crates -- opening those cartons and he's running backwards and forwards and that (unintelligible) flying.
How big a band was it?

The boy's cousin on drums, I picked up a clarinet band, Holt was on the trombone, I was on the trumpet -- not too many. Just that piano -- no, no piano -- drums, trumpet, trombone and clarinet. We played such things as 'Storm and Sunshine' and 'Chicago Tribune March', you know. We had those. Re-de-le- -- you know, you know how they go.

And we play those things and it's funny, this man would really -- he'd really sell that medicine. He'd have his hands full -- you wouldn't be able to do that now because the guys would be out there to stick him up, trying to --
Yeah, had his hands full of money. He'd bring that back and he'd run out there and be selling and get moremoney and bring it back and we're just playing and people are buying that medicine.
You just barnstormed through the south?
Yeah, we would go -- he would set up and we would play three to four weeks at one time in the same place.
